title: Fibrewise dense affine opens have Cartier boundary over a normal base
statement: Let $T$ be an affine locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] whose local rings are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $f:X\to T$ be a smooth separated morphism of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion. Let $U\subseteq X$ be an affine open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Suppose that, for every $t\in T$, the open $U_t=U\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ is dense in $X_t=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field]. Then the reduced induced closed subscheme $D=(X\setminus U)_{\mathrm{red}}$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] is an effective Cartier divisor: its ideal is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. In particular, $|D|=|X|\setminus|U|$. The case $U=X$, with $D$ empty and ideal $\mathcal O_X$, is included. No group law on $X$, regularity of $T$, or properness is assumed.

source.place: Guo, Divisors on coherent schemes and homogeneous spaces, Proposition 3.3, implication (iii) to (i) and (ii), printed pp.5--6; the Noetherian Ramanujam--Samuel argument in the last paragraph (EGA IV4, Proposition 21.14.3). Read online in the March 31, 2026 version; local copy WANTED. This is the locally Noetherian specialization, also for a normal affine base with finitely many disjoint integral components.

proof.text: The affine locally Noetherian $T$ is Noetherian (an affine scheme is quasi-compact). Finite presentation implies finite type by forgetting the finitely many relations in each affine presentation, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian. By [lem-sc-separated-over-affine-scheme-separated], $X$ is separated. For each $t$, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3) makes $X_t\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ finitely presented, hence finite type; the residue field is Noetherian, so the same Noetherian lemma makes $X_t$ Noetherian.

source.place: Tags 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), 01TS (lemma-base-change-finite-presentation); Schemes Tags 01KN and 01KU for separatedness over an affine base.

proof.text: The open $U$ is dense in $X$: a nonempty open $V\subseteq X$ meets some fibre in a nonempty open $V_t$, and density of $U_t$ gives $V_t\cap U_t\ne\varnothing$, hence $V\cap U\ne\varnothing$. Write $F=|X|\setminus|U|$. By [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components], $F$ has finitely many distinct irreducible components $Z_1,\ldots,Z_r$. By [lem-sfb-affine-open-boundary-codimension-one], each generic point $\xi_i$ satisfies $\dim\mathcal O_{X,\xi_i}=1$. All its hypotheses hold: $X$ is separated locally Noetherian by step 1, and $U$ is affine and dense.

No inverse image of $Z_i$ contains a fibre component. Indeed fix $t$ and list the finitely many irreducible components $C_1,\ldots,C_m$ of $X_t$, using [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components] and step 1. For each $j$, the open $O_j=X_t\setminus\bigcup_{k\ne j}C_k$ is nonempty and contained in $C_j$: otherwise irreducibility would force $C_j\subseteq C_k$ for some $k\ne j$. If $C_j$ lay in the inverse image of $Z_i\subseteq F$, this nonempty open would miss the dense $U_t$, a contradiction. Empty fibres require no argument.

source.place: Tag 0BA8 and the displayed elementary finite-component argument; verifies the fibre-support hypothesis of EGA IV4 21.14.3(i).

proof.text: Give each $Z_i$ its reduced induced structure. Apply [lem-sfb-ramanujam-samuel-prime-divisor] with $S=T$, $Y=X$ and $Z=Z_i$. The base is normal locally Noetherian as assumed; $f$ is smooth; step 2 supplies irreducibility and codimension one; step 3 supplies avoidance of every fibre component. Thus its ideal $\mathcal I_i$ has, near every point, a non-zero-divisor generator $a_i$. This use is for individual prime boundary components, not for the whole reduced boundary.

source.place: Guo Proposition 3.3, final proof paragraph, invoking EGA IV4 Proposition 21.14.3(i) on prime cycles.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal I_F$ be the reduced ideal of $F$ from [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Its pointwise vanishing definition gives $\mathcal I_F=\bigcap_i\mathcal I_i$: vanishing on a finite union means vanishing on each member. Fix $x\in X$ and omit the components not containing $x$ by shrinking. The remaining stalk ideals $\mathfrak p_i=(a_i)$ in $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ are distinct incomparable prime ideals, since they cut out the distinct reduced irreducible components through $x$. Explicitly, on an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}B$, each such component is $V(\mathfrak q_i)$ for a prime $\mathfrak q_i\subseteq\mathfrak m_x$, and the inverse image of $\mathfrak q_iB_{\mathfrak m_x}$ in $B$ is $\mathfrak q_i$. Thus localization preserves their distinctness and incomparability. For incomparable principal primes, $\bigcap_i(a_i)=(\prod_i a_i)$: if $b=a_1c\in(a_j)$ for $j>1$, then $a_1\notin(a_j)$, so primality forces $c\in(a_j)$; induction proves the formula. Finite intersections commute with stalks by choosing one common neighbourhood for finitely many germs. Therefore $(\mathcal I_F)_x=(\prod_i a_i)$. The product is a non-zero-divisor, since multiplication by each factor is injective. Choose a neighbourhood where all the $a_i$ generate their ideals; the same ideal calculation at each stalk there gives $\mathcal I_F=(\prod_i a_i)$. These neighbourhoods cover $X$, so $D=F_{\mathrm{red}}$ is an effective Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Its support is $F$ by the reduced-subscheme statement. If $r=0$, the empty intersection is $\mathcal O_X$ and the empty product is $1$, giving the empty Cartier divisor, including $U=X$ and $X=\varnothing$.
